name: Shanghai
summary: Start with the Bund and cross to Lujiazui for the skyline contrast. Spend another day around Yuyuan and the older neighbourhoods rather than repeatedly crossing the river.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are often pleasant; summer is hot and humid with storm risk, and national holidays bring crowds.
arrival: Pudong and Hongqiao airports have different city connections; follow the route for your actual airport.
gettingAround: Metro is extensive; prepare mobile payment if useful and keep a cash/card backup.
cashTip: Keep some yuan for payment failures; many venues favour mobile payment.
foodTip: Try xiaolongbao and shengjianbao; soup dumplings are hot inside and often contain pork.
buyTip: Tea, stationery and locally designed goods are practical; bargain novelty markets do not guarantee authenticity.
baseArea: People’s Square or a central metro corridor.

connections.note: Fast trains roughly 4.5–6 hours; compare the exact service and stations.

whyVisit: Shanghai’s three-star innovative tasting counter, a long-standing fixture of the city’s dining scene.
The MICHELIN Guide awards it Three MICHELIN Stars (exceptional cuisine), the guide’s highest award.
visitFlow: Book through the restaurant’s own site or official booking partner as soon as your dates are set.
Share allergies and dietary needs when booking; tasting menus are hard to change on the night.
Allow about three hours and plan a taxi or short walk back.
items.tradeoffs: Among the most expensive meals of a trip, and tables can sell out weeks or months ahead. Menus are set by the kitchen.
